entries.title: Draft: dependence-aware bad-site bound
entries.statement: DRAFT author-checked supporting bound, independent audit pending. For a binary field on Z^2 with independence of sigma-fields on index sets at infinity-norm distance greater than integer R>=0, and each bad-site probability <=q in [0,1], the probability that m>=1 distinct specified sites are all bad is <=q^ceil(m/(R+1)^2). Both coordinate residues modulo R+1 supply a jointly independent subfamily. Pairwise independence alone is insufficient.
assumptions: Strong R-dependence, not only pairwise independence

entries.title: Draft: explicit finite-dependent block threshold
entries.statement: DRAFT author-checked supporting estimate, independent audit pending. For the strongly R-dependent binary field on Z^2 with bad probability <=q, put K=(R+1)^2 and t=8*q^(1/K). If t<1, the probability that 0 belongs to an infinite nearest-neighbor good component is at least 1-q-9*t*(1+t)/(1-t)^3. In particular q<=800^(-K) yields probability >9/10. The proof uses enclosing bad star-cycles and multiplies probabilities only for an independent color subfamily.
assumptions: Nearest-neighbor good components and star-neighbor bad cycles

entries.title: Draft: local anchor certificate and critical lower bound
entries.statement: DRAFT author-checked conditional reduction, independent audit pending. For independent nearest-neighbor bond percolation on Z^d, d>=2, take plane block centers c_z=L*(z_1,z_2,0,...,0), seed boxes S_z=c_z+[-L,L]^d, and outer boxes D_z(M)=c_z+[-M,M]^d, integers M>=L>=1. Select h_z as the first vertex in S_z reaching the boundary of D_z(M) internally. G_z requires h_z and its four neighboring anchors to exist and h_z to connect to each inside D_z(M+L). Put R=floor(2*(M+L)/L). If p0>0 and P_p0(G_0^c)<800^(-(R+1)^2), finite-product continuity preserves the strict margin at some p1<p0 and compatible anchors give theta_d(p1)>0. Hence the critical failure probability for every fixed pair is at least this threshold. This does not prove critical nonpercolation.
assumptions: Same deterministic finite anchor rule in all neighboring events
Supporting box contains every test and connection
Strict threshold margin for lowering p

entries.title: Unproved: critical dependence-matched anchor estimate
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT, no theorem or solved claim. On independent nearest-neighbor bond percolation on Z^d, take centers c_z=L*(z_1,z_2,0,...,0), seeds S_z=c_z+[-L,L]^d, and D_z(M)=c_z+[-M,M]^d, integers M>=L>=1. Let h_z be the first seed vertex reaching the boundary of D_z(M) internally, using one fixed offset order. G_z requires h_z and its four neighboring anchors to exist and h_z to connect to each inside D_z(M+L). A proof route to theta_d(p_c)=0 for a fixed d in {3,...,10} would need to derive from hypothetical theta_d(p_c)>0 a finite pair with P_pc(G_0^c)<800^(-(floor(2*(M+L)/L)+1)^2). Unique infinite-cluster stabilization supplies only lim_L lim_M P_pc(G_0^c)=0. It supplies no estimate matching the increasing dependence range. A uniform fixed-aspect-ratio high-probability connection estimate would suffice, but remains unproved in this packet. Current openness of the full target is UNKNOWN.
assumptions: Iterated limit is not a joint-scale rate

entries.title: Draft: counterexample to a scale-selection inference
entries.statement: DRAFT author-checked numerical-family counterexample to a logical inference, independent audit pending. For integers M>=L>=1, let q_fake(L,M)=1 when M<L*2^L and q_fake(L,M)=2^(-L) otherwise. This is nonincreasing in M for each fixed L and lim_L lim_M q_fake=0. Nevertheless q_fake(L,M)>800^(-(floor(2*(M+L)/L)+1)^2) for every finite pair. Thus an iterated vanishing failure limit alone cannot supply a dependence-matched block certificate. No percolation realization of q_fake is asserted.
assumptions: No percolation counterexample or novelty claim
